ink.purpose: The countdown readout, and nothing else.

text-muted.purpose: Secondary and supporting text; the most used colour in the app.

action.purpose: The ordinary confirming action. Never carries state meaning.

accent.purpose: Marks the series or event currently running.

shown.purpose: Signal: the target is shown. Fixed meaning, never decorative.

stop.purpose: Signal: the target is hidden, and the colour of Cancel.

warn.purpose: Signal: no delay armed, and startup advisories.

display.purpose: The countdown digits alone. Scales up with the viewport, never down.

label.purpose: Uppercase caption above or beside a value. The tell that something is a label, not content.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Modal dialogs only. Things that genuinely float above the page.

shadows.name: response
shadows.purpose: Hover and active feedback on an interactive card.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: The running series. Neutral, never tinted to match the accent.

shadows.name: focus-action
shadows.purpose: Focus ring on a blue control.

shadows.name: focus-stop
shadows.purpose: Focus ring on the Cancel button.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Default transition for hover, background and border changes.

motion.name: pulse
motion.purpose: The countdown tick. Suppressed under prefers-reduced-motion.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The confirming action: Save, Add, Create. One per view at most.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #2563eb; border: 1px solid #2563eb; color: #fff; padding: 0.4rem 0.75rem; min-height: 40px; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.9rem; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #1d4ed8; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #2563eb; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Default Button
components.description: The neutral majority. Every non-confirming, non-destructive action.
components.css: .ds-btn-default { background: #fff; border: 1px solid #ccc; color: #213547; padding: 0.4rem 0.75rem; min-height: 40px; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.9rem; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-default:hover { background: #f3f4f6; } .ds-btn-default:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #2563eb; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Destructive Button
components.description: Delete and remove. Outlined rather than filled, so it is hard to hit by accident on a touch screen.
components.css: .ds-btn-destructive { background: #fff; border: 1px solid #dc2626; color: #dc2626; padding: 0.4rem 0.75rem; min-height: 40px; border-radius: 4px; font-size: 0.9rem; white-space: nowrap; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-destructive:hover { background: #fee2e2; } .ds-btn-destructive:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #2563eb; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Countdown Go Button
components.description: Start Now, in the countdown dialog. Green-700 because white on green-600 is 3.3:1.
components.css: .ds-btn-go { background: #15803d; color: #fff; border: none; padding: 0.75rem 1.5rem; min-height: 48px; border-radius: 8px; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.2s ease; } .ds-btn-go:hover { background: #166534; transform: translateY(-1px); box-shadow: 0 4px 12px rgba(22, 163, 74, 0.3); } .ds-btn-go:active { transform: translateY(0); } .ds-btn-go:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(22, 163, 74, 0.3); }

components.name: State Badge
components.description: Reports one piece of device state on the run board. Tinted ground, 2px signal border, uppercase caption.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.5rem; padding: 0 0.75rem; min-height: 36px; border-radius: 6px; font-size: 0.9rem; box-sizing: border-box; } .ds-badge-label { font-size: 0.75rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; font-weight: 600; opacity: 0.8; line-height: 1; } .ds-badge-shown { background: #dcfce7; color: #14532d; border: 2px solid #16a34a; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Every field in the program editor and settings. Inherits the body face so it never drifts.
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.2rem; } .ds-field-label { font-size: 0.75rem; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; font-weight: 600; color: #6b7280; } .ds-input { padding: 0.35rem 0.5rem; border: 1px solid #ccc; border-radius: 4px; font: inherit; font-size: 0.9rem; background: #fff; min-height: 40px; box-sizing: border-box; } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #2563eb; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Navigation Tab
components.description: Sticky top navigation. Stretches to fill the bar on a phone, sits at natural width above 768px.
components.html: RunProgramsAudios
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; gap: 0.25rem; padding: 0.5rem 1rem; background: #fff; border-bottom: 1px solid #eee; } .ds-link { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; min-height: 40px; padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem; border-radius: 4px; color: inherit; text-decoration: none; white-space: nowrap; flex: 1 1 auto; transition: background-color 0.2s; } .ds-link:hover { background: #f0f0f0; } .ds-link-active { font-weight: bold; background: #e0e0e0; }

components.name: Control Board
components.description: The page's primary container. Flat at rest: a border and a tone change, no resting shadow.
components.css: .ds-board { background: #fff; border: 1px solid #e5e7eb; border-radius: 8px; padding: 1rem; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1rem; } .ds-board-header { display: flex; justify-content: space-between; align-items: center; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 1rem; border-bottom: 1px solid #eee; padding-bottom: 0.75rem; } .ds-board-title { margin: 0; font-size: 1.25rem; color: #333; }

components.name: Countdown Readout
components.description: The one number read at arm's length. Near-black at 17.4:1, tabular, scaling up with the viewport.
components.css: .ds-countdown-wrap { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 1rem; padding: 2rem; background: #fff; border-radius: 12px; box-shadow: 0 25px 50px -12px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.25); } .ds-countdown-label { font-size: 1rem; color: #4b5563; font-weight: 500; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; } .ds-countdown { font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: clamp(4.5rem, 24vw, 7rem); font-weight: 700; color: #111827; line-height: 1; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.name: Timeline Event Chip
components.description: One event in a series: duration, command and cumulative time on a line. Reflows four to five per row on a phone.
components.html: 2.5s · show · 00:03.51.0s · hide · 00:04.5
components.css: .ds-series { display: flex; gap: 6px; flex-wrap: wrap; padding: 1rem; background: #fafafa; border: 1px solid #eee; border-radius: 8px; } .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; padding: 0.4rem 0.6rem; border: 1px solid #ddd; border-radius: 6px; background: #fff; font-size: 0.8rem; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-chip-show { background: #dcfce7; border-color: #16a34a; color: #14532d; } .ds-chip-hide { background: #fee2e2; border-color: #fca5a5; color: #7f1d1d; }

narrative.overview:
This is range equipment that happens to have a screen. It is read standing up, outdoors, in daylight, by someone who is about to run a live firing exercise and has better things to look at than a user interface. Every visual decision answers to that scene: grey by default, colour only where colour carries a safety meaning, and type sized so the one number that matters can be read at arm's length without walking to the phone.

The system is deliberately quiet. There is no brand expression competing for attention, because the three signal colours - green, red, amber - have fixed operational meanings and must be impossible to mistake for decoration. When a surface looks plain here, that is the design working, not the design missing.

Density is medium and consistent: one control height for the whole app, one breakpoint, one type ramp. The interface should feel like a well-labelled panel of switches, where nothing moves unless the state moved.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral greys carry structure; hue is reserved for state
One control height (40px pointer, 44px touch) governs every row
Numbers are tabular so a readout never reflows as it counts
Flat at rest - depth is a response, not an ornament
Legibility in daylight outranks visual interest, always

rules.name: The Three Signals Rule
rules.body: Green means the target is shown, red means it is hidden, amber means no delay is armed. No other element may use those hues for any other purpose. If a new state needs a colour and is not one of those three things, it uses indigo or a grey.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: The palette is the Tailwind scale. Two earlier families are still present in the code - the Vite starter purple (#646cff) and the Material greens (#e8f5e9, #a5d6a7) - and are being retired. Do not add to them.

rules.name: The Readable Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal colours are chosen for contrast, not brightness. White text sits on green-700 (#15803d), never green-600, because white on green-600 measures 3.3:1 and fails AA. Any new coloured surface must clear 4.5:1 for its text before it ships.

rules.name: The Arm's Length Rule
rules.body: The countdown grows with the viewport instead of shrinking with it. A phone held at the firing line is further from the eye than a laptop on a desk, so 24vw is the floor of the readout, not its ceiling.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any number that changes in place is font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums. A readout that jitters as its digits change is a readout nobody trusts.

rules.name: The No Nested Scroller Rule
rules.body: The document scrolls; panels do not. A flex child with overflow-y: auto also computes overflow-x: auto, which silently clipped the programs and audios tables off the right edge on a phone. Wide content gets its own explicitly scrollable wrapper.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: A card gets a border, not a shadow. If you are reaching for box-shadow on a resting surface, the answer is a tone change or a border.

rules.name: The Neutral Elevation Rule
rules.body: Shadows are black at low alpha. A shadow tinted to match its element's accent colour is decoration pretending to be depth.

rules.name: The Side-Tab Ban
rules.body: No thick coloured border on one edge of a card. It is the most recognisable tell of machine-generated UI, and this system says warning with a tinted ground and a full hairline border instead.

dos: Do reserve green, red and amber for target shown, target hidden, and no delay armed. Anything else that needs colour uses indigo or a grey.
Do put every interactive control at var(--rt-control-height) so mixed rows line up and touch targets stay at 44px on a phone.
Do use font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on any number that updates in place.
Do give every focusable element a visible :focus-visible outline - 2px solid #2563eb, 2px offset.
Do check 4.5:1 contrast for text on any new coloured ground before shipping it. This system has already had ten failures found and fixed.
Do give wide content (tables, timelines) its own scrollable wrapper rather than letting a layout container scroll.
donts: Don't put a thick coloured border on one side of a card.
Don't put a resting shadow on a card. Use a border and a tone change.
Don't tint a shadow to match its element's colour.
Don't add overflow-y: auto to a flex layout container; it computes overflow-x: auto too and will clip content off the right edge.
Don't put white text on green-600 (#16a34a) - 3.3:1. Use green-700.
Don't introduce a fifth button style. There are four, and twelve files already redefine them; the next one should reuse, not add.
Don't scale the countdown down on small screens. It is read from further away there, not closer.
